hints.content: A relative minimum point is a point that is lower than all other graph points around it. It's like the lowest point on a "valley."

The graph has two relative minimum points in the given section. One at $(-3,4)$, and one at $(5,-6)$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes each scale by one. A function decreases at a non linear rate from the point negative seven, eight to the point negative three, four. Then it increases at a non linear rate to negative zero, six. A line segment connects zero, six to two, negative three. Then it decreases at a non linear rate to five, negative six. Then it increases at a non linear rate to eight, negative three.
